Maintenance Report — MNT-0089-001

Asset: WELL-0089 (SW-24 Well 089, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 25 Nov 2022 08:00 · Finished: 26 Nov 2022 10:00 · Well stopped for this job: 26 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Megan Ward, Daniel Foster · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0089-0006 on 2022-11-24 Report written: 28 Nov 2022

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0089-0006 at 15:45 on 2022-11-24 found crude oil on the pad: about 6.1% of the pad area, estimated 2.3 bbl. The inspector noted: "Oil sheen around cellar." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 2.8 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to the flanged flowline connection at the wellhead cellar.

Root cause

A failed gasket on the flange where the flowline leaves the wellhead.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Cleaned free oil out of the cellar.
  2. Unbolted the flange and removed the failed gasket.
  3. Fitted a new gasket and new bolts, torqued to specification.
  4. Excavated the stained soil around the cellar.

Summary of the fix: replaced the flange gasket and bolts and remediated soil.

Testing and return to service

Pressure-tested the repaired section at 270 psi (1.25 × the flowline's maximum operating pressure of 216 psi) and held it for 4 hours with no pressure drop (WS-05). The well was returned to production.

Spill clean-up and waste

  • About 2.1 m³ of stained soil excavated, bagged and sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0089-001 (WS-06).
  • 2 soil samples taken around the spill; the highest result after clean-up was 0.63% TPH, below the 1.0% target (SR-03).

Maintenance Report — MNT-0089-002

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0089-0009 showed the wellhead at 11.1 °C with the air at 10.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).

  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0089-009

Asset: WELL-0089 (SW-24 Well 089, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 31 Dec 2023 08:00 · Finished: 17 Jan 2024 16:00 · Well stopped for this job: 416 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price Triggered by: inspection INS-0089-0063 on 2023-12-28 Report written: 19 Jan 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that oil was dripping from the gearbox onto the pump jack base. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0089-0063 showed the wellhead at 7.9 °C with the air at 8.1 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. The input shaft seal was worn and the gearbox oil level was below the sight glass. The well stayed shut in for about 15 days longer than the repair itself because the job had to wait for a weekday contractor slot.

Root cause

Seal wear, made worse by heat and a low oil level.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Drained the gearbox oil into a closed container.
  2. Replaced the input and output shaft seals.
  3. Cleaned the base and absorbed the spilled oil.
  4. Refilled with the specified gear oil to the correct level.

Summary of the fix: replaced gearbox seals and topped up oil.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 1 hour and checked both shafts for leaks: none found. The well was returned to production.

Waste

  • Used gear oil and oily pads sent to an approved disposal site under waste manifest WM-0089-009 (WS-06).
